glosses: Personne qui regarde à la suite tous les épisodes d’une série télévisée ou d’un groupe de films.
One who binge-watches a television programme.

examples.text: The market is adjusting to binge-watchers. Family Video has seasons of "24," "Prison Break" and "Boston Legal" available on DVD.
But its in-house translators have raced to append Chinese subtitles, finishing Chinese captions for two new episodes a day since then. That hasn’t stopped some binge-watchers from racing ahead.

The un-killable Counter Terrorist Unit agent Jack Bauer, who in the interim has remained hugely popular with DVD "binge-watchers", returns after a four-year hiatus to try to foil another terrorist plot that threatens to bring about the end of Western civilisation as we know it.

glosses: Regarder à la suite tous les épisodes d’une série télévisée ou d’un groupe de films.

examples.text: Comment continuer à binge-watcher quand on devient parent ?

Bon des mauvaises journées ça arrive à tout le monde… Moi perso j’opte pour le roulage en boule dans la couette et je binge-watche des séries jusqu’au lendemain. Youtube c’est pas mal aussi pour se perdre.

glosses: To watch multiple episodes of a television programme in a short period of time.

examples.text: Thankfully, due to the power of BBC iPlayer, I was able to binge-watch the whole series of The Great British Sewing Bee last Sunday.
"People come to shows, but not in the numbers we all hope for. We must give audiences a reason to tear away from the Internet and binge-watching Doctor Who."
"Oh, that was good, too," she [Hillary Clinton] said, describing a little self-consciously how she and her husband Bill "totally binge-watched" the first season of House of Cards.
